messages:
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] High 5xx spike detected for route /v1/generate -> us-east-1 region. 5xx rate 12% (baseline ~0.2%). Smart-routing fallbacks firing rapidly; suspected routing oscillation. Paging @eric_k and infra on-call.

eric_k: Ack, I'm on it. Pulling routing and DNS logs now.

maya_g: I'm available — infra on-call. Will help with edge/CDN.

eric_k: Quick findings: LB -> smart-router -> origin resolution shows inconsistent DNS TTL behavior. Route53 has TTL=30s but CDN/edge caches show stale A records (~3600s). Dig and curl below.

```
$ dig +short model-us-east.prod.rw-inference.net @8.8.8.8
52.18.34.12
52.18.34.13
# next query (10s later) still returns 52.18.34.12 although route53 changed to 18.205.44.99
```

sasha_p: I'm seeing a model-variant mismatch thrown in runtime logs. Some edges are proxying to model variant "redwood-large-quant" while production clients expect "redwood-large". Runtime responds with a signature error -> 502 -> that triggers Route53 health check failover -> smart-routing moves traffic to backup region which itself still has cached DNS pointing to the old edge -> requests bounce back. Looks like a variant compatibility check isn't in the routing policy.

eric_k: Routing logs snippet (trimmed):

```
2024-10-21T12:34:01Z route=prod smart-routing: choose us-east-1 primary
2024-10-21T12:34:02Z runtime: 502 runtime.signature_mismatch model=redwood-large expected=redwood-large
2024-10-21T12:34:03Z route=prod smart-routing: failover to eu-west-1
2024-10-21T12:34:04Z route=prod smart-routing: failback to us-east-1
```

ryan_ops: Rolling mitigation in progress: paused failover for route `route.rw.prod` (set policy.failover=false), pinned primary to us-east-1 to stop oscillation.

maya_g: Purged CDN edge cache for affected host via Cloudflare API (purged hostname and A-record cache). Ran a quick validation: `curl -H "Host: model-us-east.prod.rw-inference.net" https://edge-verify/health` returned 200 after purge.

```
$ curl -s -I -H "Host: model-us-east.prod.rw-inference.net" https://edge-verify/health
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Server: cloudflare
CF-Cache-Status: MISS
```

oncall-lia: Handoff in ~30m. What's customer impact and any open blockers for me?

eric_k: Impact snapshot: approximately 8% of token-generation requests saw increased latency/timeouts during the window; ~3 enterprise customers reported streaming disconnects and timeouts (tenant ids: enterprise-acct-42, enterprise-acct-99, enterprise-acct-171). No data exfiltration suspected. We're tracking SLA thresholds.

customer-success-bot: CS notified for affected tenants, message draft prepared and queued for review.

sasha_p: Root cause hypothesis: Route53 health checks experienced legitimate failures because runtime returned 502s (due to model variant mismatch after a partial rollout of quantized variant). Route53 then updated the failover target, but the CDN/edge did not honor the low TTL in all edge caches, leading to stale A records at some PoPs. Smart-routing lacked a model-variant compatibility guard — so when traffic moved to a fallback region, some edge nodes still resolved to IPs serving the incompatible variant, causing more 502s and the loop.

eric_k: Actions taken so far:
- paused smart-routing automatic failover for the route
- pinned route to us-east-1 primary
- CDN edge purge executed across major PoPs
- restarted inference runtime processes on affected us-east nodes to clear cached model metadata (k8s restarts)

Commands run:
```
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime-us-east
# cloudflare purge via API script run against host model-us-east.prod.rw-inference.net
```

maya_g: Reached out to CDN provider support — they confirmed an internal edge invalidation delay for A-record caches when origin IPs shift quickly. They recommended an immediate global purge (we executed) and will investigate why TTL override occurred.

ryan_ops: Short-term config change: adding a model-variant compatibility check to the routing decision engine to prevent routing to endpoints that advertise an incompatible model tag. Will push a small canary rule and monitor.

oncall-lia: Taking the next shift. Anything I should watch on the dashboard?

eric_k: Watch `5xx_rate by route`, `smart_routing_failover_count`, and `edge_dns_cache_miss_rate`. I've annotated the incident and left runbook pointers. Post-incident follow-ups: postmortem owner, add unit tests for policy, update runbook to include CDN purge + DNS verification, escalate DNS provider if TTL enforcement is not fixed.

maya_g: I'll open a Jira ticket for provider escalation and add the CDN provider contact thread. Also will add an alert: `smart_routing_fallback_rate > 1% for 5m`.

customer-success-bot: Customer comms sent for enterprise-acct-42 and enterprise-acct-99 with ETA and blameless summary draft.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: recovered — error rate returned to baseline ~12 minutes after mitigations. Incident duration: ~42 minutes. Status: degraded -> recovered. Summary: DNS/CDN cache inconsistency combined with routing policy missing model-variant compatibility check caused failover oscillation and 5xx spike.

eric_k: Thanks everyone. Postmortem owner: sasha_p. Oncall next: oncall-lia. Please add any missing notes to the ticket. :thumbsup:
